family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Ignore the flower at first and look underwater: Cabomba has opposite fan-shaped leaves repeatedly divided into fine segments. Then confirm the small 3-merous surface flower.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Rooted submerged aquatic with slender branching stems and strongly divided leaves; floating leaves may appear near flowering shoots.
family_diagnostics.flowers: Small solitary surface flowers, typically with 3 sepals + 3 petals in the local Cabomba anchor.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Opposite fan-shaped submerged leaves are much more diagnostic than a generic 'feathery aquatic plant' impression.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Cabomba teaches a clean aquatic ID workflow: underwater leaf architecture first, tiny surface flower second.

steps.title: 1 · Find opposite fan leaves
steps.look_for: Opposite leaves shaped like fans and repeatedly divided into fine segments.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the strongest field character for the local family anchor.

steps.title: 2 · Check the leaf arrangement
steps.look_for: Leaves paired opposite one another rather than arranged in large whorls.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates Cabomba from several finely divided submerged lookalikes.

steps.title: 3 · Find the surface flower
steps.look_for: A small white-to-purplish flower with three sepals and three petals.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirms the submerged foliage with reproductive structure.

comparisons.title: Cabomba vs Limnophila
comparisons.rule: Cabomba has opposite fan-shaped leaves; Limnophila typically has finely divided leaves in whorls.
